summary: The ingredients exist separately for planktonic foraminifera: species-labelled image sets (Endless Forams, 26,663 + training images on Zenodo, CC BY 4.0), SSU sequences (6,975 foraminiferal 18S records in GenBank; PR2 v5.1.1 curated taxonomy) and 196,776 dated fossil occurrences in PBDB. No dataset joins morphology, molecular phylogeny and time for the same taxa, and nothing comparable was found for radiolaria or ciliates; Neotoma holds no foraminiferal datasets.
next_step: Build a species-level table for planktonic forams joining Endless Forams shape descriptors (via AutoMorph outlines), a PR2/GenBank 18S phylogeny and PBDB first/last occurrences; then pre-register a test of whether morphologically near-identical species pairs are more often non-sister than in a character-rich comparison group.
obstacles_confirmed: Morphological descriptions and molecular samples rarely come from the same individuals: image sets and sequence databases are disjoint.
Soft-bodied infusoria lack a fossil record: no ciliate morphology or occurrence dataset surfaced; the deep-time half is testable only for forams/radiolaria.
Neotoma, suggested by one assessor, is Quaternary and returned no foraminiferal datasets.
